report:
Reviewed the full definition-identity claim, all four ordinary implementation associations (resolver, ribs, symbol wrappers, resolved types), and the sole TODO test. Captured the typed-body representation as additional context for downstream reference storage. No production or test sources were changed.

The claim separates discovery spelling/path from successful semantic reference identity and requires aliases and alternate routes to preserve the same definition. resolve_path returns Resolution::Sym around the symbol found by module/path lookup, rather than wrapping the spelling used to reach it. Named-use resolution follows the imported path and returns its target symbol; glob traversal likewise carries target symbols. Candidate deduplication uses Symbol equality, not names. The new ambiguity audit compares generated and glob target identities; it examines the binding item's origin without allocating a replacement definition for that binding. Thus provenance is used for ambiguity classification but not substituted for semantic identity.

ribs.rs represents local variables by body LocalId, generic parameters by GenericParam, and item references by Symbol; it copies stored entries instead of re-interning by the queried name. symbol/mod.rs wraps the existing local tracked identity or external SymExt in canonical kind wrappers, with derived equality/hash and conversions retaining the payload. External named-child lookup uses exported edge names and namespaces for discovery but constructs SymExt from the defining crate/index/kind; aliases do not enter that key. ty.rs stores Symbol in ADT applications, TypeAliasSymbol in named/opaque/projection identities, and TraitSymbol in trait references, preserving definitions while keeping substitutions separate. The additionally captured typed-body context agrees: PathResolution::Def stores Symbol, resolved calls store FnSymbol, and resolved fields carry owner identity plus field index. Those body-specific contracts have their own existing associations; this capture does not claim broader body coverage for this anchor.

The associated representation_spec::todo::symbols_definition_identity explicitly defers the distinct-path/same-symbol and equal-spelling/different-scope resolution matrix, noting that displayed examples do not establish identity. This remains a substantive verification gap: snapshots of equal names can conceal different internal symbols, and direct identity/equality assertions across aliases, paths and separate scopes are the needed prerequisite. No ordinary test is associated with this anchor, and this review does not promote other anchors' output examples into evidence. There are no N/A entries. The ordinary code structure supports the intended identity boundary; accepting the explicit TODO does not assert that the complete matrix has been tested. This review ran start/read/record commands only and did not execute new behavioral tests. No new violation was identified in the changed resolver; no edits requested.
